2609.29007.title: When Does Action Credit Need Updating?
2609.29007.paper_summary: Tool-using agents are continually updated with new interaction data. After each policy update, however, previously estimated action credits may become stale. Recomputing them from scratch can require many additional tool calls and environment interactions, making repeated updates increasingly expensive. We ask a simple question: when does historical action credit actually need to be updated? Our key observation is that a change in action value does not necessarily imply a change in the decision. Historical credit can still be useful as long as policy-induced drift is too small to overturn the existing action ranking. Building on this idea, we introduce pairwise branch sensitivity to capture how strongly a policy update affects the downstream regions that distinguish two candidate actions. We then derive a first-order anchored credit-transport estimator that updates historical credit using old interventional trajectories, and propose a Decision-Sufficient Credit Gate (DSC-Gate) that chooses whether to reuse, transport, or resample credit. Experiments show that branch sensitivity explains credit drift substantially better than global policy distance. With sufficient historical data, credit transport reduces estimation error, while its benefit to decision making is concentrated on updates that affect action-distinguishing branches. On a fully independent test set, DSC-Gate changes mean regret by only +0.00004 relative to a gap-based gate while reducing mean new tool steps from 472 to 286, a 39.4% reduction. We observe the same pattern after a real tool-agent parameter update. Overall, our results show that agents do not need to recompute action credit after every policy update: much of the historical evidence can be reused or cheaply corrected, reducing the additional interaction required to keep action decisions up to date.
2609.29007.paper_summary_zh: 使用工具的代理不斷更新新的互動數據。 然而，在每次策略更新後，先前估計的行動信用可能會變得過時。 從頭開始重新計算它們可能需要許多額外的工具調用和環境互動，這使得重複更新變得越來越昂貴。 我們提出一個簡單的問題：歷史行動信用何時實際需要更新？ 我們的關鍵觀察是，行動價值的變化並不一定意味著決策的變化。 只要政策引起的漂移過小，以至於無法推翻現有的行動排名，歷史信用仍然可以是有用的。 基於這個想法，我們引入了成對分支敏感度，以捕捉策略更新對區分兩個候選行動的下游區域的影響程度。 然後，我們推導出一種一階錨定信用傳輸估計器，利用舊的干預軌跡來更新歷史信用，並提出了一個決策充分信用門（DSC-Gate），用於選擇是重用、傳輸還是重新抽樣信用。 實驗顯示，分支敏感度對信用漂移的解釋明顯優於全局策略距離。 在有足夠歷史數據的情況下，信用傳輸減少了估計誤差，而其對決策的好處集中在影響行動區分分支的更新上。 在一個完全獨立的測試集上，DSC-Gate相對於基於間隙的門僅改變了平均懊悔+0.00004，同時將平均新工具步驟從472減少到286，減少了39.4%。 我們在一次真實的工具代理參數更新後觀察到相同的模式。 總體而言，我們的結果顯示，代理不需要在每次策略更新後重新計算行動信用：大量的歷史證據可以重用或廉價修正，減少了保持行動決策最新所需的額外互動。
